newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mixed in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mixed in quiet trading.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in quiet trade on Monday, with investors awaiting economic data out later in the week for clues about the timing of the Bank of Canada's next rate hike, analysts said.

"The market is generally expecting the Bank (of Canada) to be increasing interest rates in the forseeable future here given the strength of the fundamentals," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management. "The Canadian statistics are becoming more prominent in people's minds."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.16 percent from 3.17 percent at Friday's close. The three-month cash T-bill traded unchanged to yield 3.16 percent.

Activity was light in the Canadian money market this morning with many accounts absent and trading largely dealer- driven. Analysts said the likelihood of another central bank tightening in the next few months is weighing on prices.
Economic reports which will be closely watched by the market include Canada's consumer price index for June out on Thursday, and Friday's merchandise and wholesale trade data.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.40 percent from a 3.41 percent at Friday's close. The one-year T-bill softened to yield 4.04 percent from 4.03 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.20 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
